source_text: δικαιοσύνης σου τὰ δικαιώματά σου φυλάξω. σύνεσιν αἰτεῖ, φησί, καὶ ταύτην οὐκ ἄκαρπον ἕξειν ἐπαγγέλλεται. οὐ γὰρ μαθήσομαι μόνον, φησίν, ἀλλὰ καὶ φυλάξω τὰ δικαιώματά σου. 215 Ps 118,10 Ἀκύλας φησὶ Μὴ ἀγνοηματίσῃς με [πρὸς ὅπερ ἐροῦμεν]. ἐπιθυμίᾳ τῇ περὶ τὸν νόμον χρώμενος δέδοικε τὴν ἀσυνεσίαν ἣ πολλοῖς τὴν σπουδὴν εἰς τοὐναντίον περιίστησιν. καὶ ἐν οἷς δοκοῦσι κατορθοῦν, ἐσφάλησαν κατὰ τὸ λεγόμενον παρὰ Σολομῶνι Ἔστιν ὁδὸς ἣ δοκεῖ παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ὀρθῆ εἶναι, τὰ δὲ τελευταῖα αὐτῆς ἔρχεται εἰς πυθμένα ᾅδου. 216 Ps 118,12b Οὐ γὰρ εὐθὺς ἀπὸ τῆς μνήμης ἡ σύνεσις ἀλλ' ἀπὸ τοῦ θείου φωτισμοῦ· δικαιώματα δὲ τὰ δικαιῶσαι δυνάμενα. 217 Ps 118,21 Μήτηρ παρανομίας ὑπερηφανία. διὰ γὰρ ταύτην οὐκ ἀνέχονται ὑπακούειν προστάγμασι θεοῦ, οἷός ἐστιν ὁ ἀπειθὴς λαὸς λέγων Οὐ κυριευθησόμεθα καὶ οὐχ ἥξομεν πρὸς σὲ ἔτι. τοῦτο δὲ λέγει τὴν αὐτοῦ προθυμίαν ἐπιδεικνὺς θεῷ τὴν πρὸς ὑπακοὴν τῶν ἐντολῶν. ὅτι συνίησιν ἐνόχους, ἐπιτιμήσει τοὺς δι' ὑπερηφανίας ἀπειθεῖς καὶ ἀνυποτάκτους. 218 Ps 118,22.23 Εὔχεται τὴν ἀληθῆ φυγεῖν ἀδοξίαν τὴν παρὰ θεῷ ἣν φοβερωτάτην ὁ κύριος ὑποδείκνυσι λέγων ἐπαισχυνθήσεσθαι τοὺς ἐπαισχυνθέντας αὐτόν· οὗ δὴ τὸ ἐναντίον ἐνδεικνύμενος ὁ νόμιμος οὗτος ἄνθρωπος ἐνταῦθα λέγει χλευαζόμενος ὑπὸ μεγάλων καὶ ὑπερηφάνων μὴ ἀφίστασθαι τῆς τῶν ἱερῶν λογίων μελέτης καὶ τῆς ὑπ' αὐτῶν διορθώσεως, καὶ μικρὸν ὕστερον Ἐλάλουν, φησίν, ἐν τοῖς μαρτυρίοις σου ἐναντίον βασιλέων καὶ οὐκ ᾐσχυνόμην· οἷός ἐστι καὶ ὁ Παῦλος λέγων Οὐ γὰρ ἐπαισχύνομαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον. 219 Ps 118,25 Ὅπερ αὐτὸς λέγει θυσίαν εἶναι θεῷ καρδίαν συντετριμμένην καὶ τεταπεινωμένην, τοῦτο νῦν πεπληρωκέναι φησὶ καταγαγὼν τὴν ψυχὴν ὥσπερ εἰς ἔδαφος καὶ ταπεινωθεὶς ἑκουσίως, ὡς περὶ τῆς ἀκουσίου λέγει ταπεινώσεως τὸ Ἐταπεινώθη εἰς χοῦν ἡ ψυχὴ ἡμῶν, ἐκολλήθη εἰς γῆν ἡ γαστὴρ 31 ἡμῶν. προσαγαγὼν οὖν ἑαυτὸν ὡς προσήκει ταπεινόν, ἀμοιβὴν ζητεῖ παρὰ θεοῦ τὴν ἐπὶ βίον ἔννομον ἀγωγὴν καὶ τὴν κατὰ λόγον θεοῦ ζωήν. ταπεινοῦ δὲ καὶ αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ μὴ ἐφ' ἑαυτοῦ τίθεσθαι τὴν ἀγαθὴν ζωὴν ἀλλὰ παρὰ θεοῦ ζητεῖν. 220 Ps 118,26.27 Μέγα τὸ πάντα πράττειν ὡς ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς θεοῦ καὶ λέγειν ταῦτα καὶ διηγεῖσθαι καὶ τὴν ἐπὶ τούτοις αἰτεῖν ἀποκάλυψιν διορθωτικὴν ἢ βεβαιωτικήν, περιέσεσθαι δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν εἰς ἄλλους ὠφέλειαν ἐκ θειοτέρας συνέσεως διαλεγομένῳ καὶ τὴν θαυμασίαν εὐεργεσίαν ἐξαγγέλλοντι τὴν θεοῦ τὴν τοῖς ὅσια πράττουσιν ἀποκειμένην. ὁ γὰρ τὰ περὶ δικαιοσύνης διδάσκων διδάσκει καὶ τὰ περὶ τοῦ τέλους, ὅπερ ἀπόκειται αὐτῇ, θαυμασίου τινὸς ὄντος καὶ παραδόξου ὅτι θεὸς μεγάλως καὶ ὑπὲρ τὴν ἀξίαν ἀμείβεται. διελέγετο καὶ Παῦλος περὶ ἐγκρατείας καὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ τοῦ κρίματος τοῦ μέλλοντος ὡς ἔμφοβον γενέσθαι τὸν ἡγεμόνα. Ἀντὶ δὲ τοῦ Ἀδολεσχήσω ὁ μὲν Ἀκύλας Ὁμιλήσω, ὁ δὲ ΣύμμαχοςἘξηγήσομαι. 221 Ps 118,36 Ἐγκειμένης τῆς καρδίας τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπιμελῶς ἐπὶ τὰ πονηρὰ ἐκ νεότητος, θεοῦ δεῖ τοῦ μετακινοῦντος αὐτὴν ἐπὶ τὰ δίκαια προστάγματα, τουτέστιν ἐνάξοντος τὸ προαιρετικὸν ἡμῶν οἰκονομίαις τε καὶ πραγμάτων καὶ θείου πνεύματος ἐλλάμψει. 222 Ps 118,37 Ματαιότης ἐστὶν ἡ περὶ τὰς θέας μανία, ἡ περὶ τῶν μηδὲ ὄντων θεωρία, καὶ ἡ κατὰ διάνοιαν δὲ ἄτοπος φαντασία ἣν καὶ σαφηνίζει ὁ Παῦλος λέγων Ἐν ματαιότητι τοῦ νοὸς αὐτῶν ἐσκοτισμένοι τῇ διανοίᾳ ὄντες ἀπηλλοτριωμένοι τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ θεοῦ. ὅρα ματαιότητα νοὸς λεγομένην ὅταν ἔχῃ τις νοῦν καὶ τούτῳ μὴ χρήσηται πρὸς τὴν τῶν ἀληθῶν θεωρίαν, ἀλλὰ παρέχει αὐτὸν τῷ δεσμεύοντι σατανᾷ. τοῦτο τοίνυν εὐχόμενός φησιν Ἀπόστρεψον τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς μου τοῦ μὴ ἰδεῖν ματαιότητας· τοῦτο γὰρ χάρις θεοῦ. οὕτω γὰρ δυνήσεται τῆς τοιαύτης κατανοήσεως ἀποστὰς ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ θεοῦ ζῆσαι, αὐτὴν βαδίζων καὶ πρὸς αὐτὴν ζωοποιούμενος· ἅμα γὰρ τὸ ὁδὸς εἶναι καὶ ζωή ἐστιν. διό φησιν ὁ σωτὴρ Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ζωή. 223 Ps 118,40b Καὶ ἐπεὶ δικαιοσύνη τοῦ πατρὸς ὁ υἱός, ὁ ἐν υἱῷ ζῆσαι βουλόμενος τοῦτό φησι· ∆ικαιοσύνη γὰρ θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν. 224 Ps 118,50 Μόνον φησὶν ἱκανὸν ἡμᾶς ἐν ταῖς κακώσεσι παραμυθεῖσθαι τὸ ζωῆς ἀληθινῆς ἔχειν ἐπαγγελίαν· τοῦθ' ἡμῖν ἐπιτέλεσον. Εἰ γὰρ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ ταύτῃ μόνον ἐν Χριστῷ ἠλπικότες ἐσμέν, ἐλεεινότεροι πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἐσμέν, ὅτι καὶ κακούμεθα νῦν καὶ οὐκ ἐπ' ἐλπίδι μελλούσης ζωῆς. ζωὴ δὲ ἡ μέλλουσά ἐστιν ἀναζώωσις, καθὸ τὴν ψυχὴν ἰδίαν ζωὴν οὐδὲ ἀληθῆ ζωὴν εἶναι
english: I will keep your statutes of righteousness. He says it asks for understanding, and it is promised that this will not be unfruitful. For I will not only learn, he says, but I will also keep your statutes (Ps 118:10).

Akyllas says, 'Let me not be ignorant' [toward what we are saying]. One using desire regarding the law fears the lack of understanding, which turns the zeal of many into the opposite. And in those things in which they seem to be upright, they have stumbled according to that which is said by Solomon: 'There is a way that seems right to men, but its end comes into the pit of Sheol' (Prov 14:12). For understanding does not come immediately from memory, but from the divine illumination; and the statutes are those capable of justifying (Ps 118:12b).

Pride is the mother of lawlessness. For through this they do not endure to obey the commands of God, such as the disobedient people who say, 'We will not be ruled, nor will we come to you anymore.' This shows his own readiness toward obeying the commandments to God. For he understands the guilty, and he will rebuke those who are disobedient and unruly through pride.

He prays to flee from the ignominy which is before God, which the Lord shows to be most fearful, saying that those who have shamed Him will be shamed (Ps 118:22). The lawful man, pointing out the opposite of this, says here mocking, [that they] are not to depart from the study of the holy oracles and the correction through them, and shortly after, he says, 'I have spoken in your testimonies against kings, and I was not ashamed' (Ps 118:23); such is also Paul, saying, 'For I am not ashamed of the gospel' (Rom 1:16).

What he himself says is to be a sacrifice to God, a broken and humbled heart, he says has now been fulfilled, having brought the soul down as to the ground and having been humbled voluntarily, just as regarding involuntary humbling it is said, 'Our soul was humbled into dust, our womb clung to the earth' (Ps 29:9). Having brought himself as becomes a humble man, he seeks from God a reward: a life-conduct according to the law and life according to the word of God (Ps 118:25). And this very thing is humbling: not to set the good life upon oneself, but to seek it from God.
To do all things greatly as in the eyes of God and to say these things and to recount (Ps 118:26-27).

And to ask for a corrective or confirming revelation regarding these things, while there remains for him also the benefit to others by conversing with a more divine understanding and announcing the wonderful benefit which God has stored up for those doing what is holy. For he who teaches concerning righteousness also teaches concerning the end, which is laid up for it, being something wonderful and unexpected, that God greatly and beyond measure rewards. Paul also conversed concerning self-control and righteousness and the judgment that is to come, as the ruler becomes a terror. Instead of 'I will not wander,' one [says] 'Akylas will preach,' and the other 'Symmachus will explain.'

If the heart of man is carefully directed toward evil from youth, it is necessary that God, by moving it toward righteous commands—that is, by leading our choice toward economies and realities and the illumination of the Holy Spirit—[intervene].

Vanity is the madness concerning visions, the contemplation concerning non-existent things, and the absurd fantasy according to the intellect, which Paul makes clear, saying, 'Being darkened in the vanity of their mind, having been alienated from the life of God' (Rom 1:21). See that 'vanity of mind' is called so when one has a mind and does not use it for the contemplation of the truths, but provides it to the binding Satan. This, therefore, he says, 'Turn my eyes away, lest I see vanity'; for this is by the grace of God. For in this way one will be able, having turned away from such an understanding, to live in the way of God, walking in it and making oneself alive by it; for at once to be the way is to be life. Therefore the Savior says, 'I am the way and the life' (John 14:6).
And since the Son is the righteousness of the Father, he says this regarding one desiring to live in the Son; for the righteousness of God is revealed in him from faith to faith (Rom 1:17).

He says only that it is sufficient for us to be comforted in afflictions to have the promise of true life; 'fulfill this for us.' For if in this life only we are hoping in Christ, we are more to be pitied than all men, because we suffer evil now and not in expectation of a life to come. But the life that is to come is a resuscitation, since the soul itself is not life, nor is it true life.

source_text: μανθάνομεν, εἴπερ οὐκ ἄνθρωπος ἡ ψυχή. εἰ γὰρ ἐν τῇ καθ' ἑαυτὴν ζωῇ τὸ ἀληθὲς εἶχε τοῦ ζῆν, οὐκ ἀναζωώσεως τὸ τεθνηκὸς ἐδεῖτο. διὸ καὶ ὁ κύριος τοὺς τεθνεῶτας θεῷ ζῆν εἶπεν ὡς οὔπω τὸ ζῆν ἔχοντας πλὴν ὅσον ἐν δυνάμει θεοῦ τοῦ ζωοποιήσαντος· καὶ ἀπολωλέναι φησὶν ἑαυτούς, εἰ μὴ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τύχοιεν, λέγων ἀναστήσειν τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ τὸ ἓν ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἀπώληται. καὶ ὁ Παῦλος ὁμοίως φησὶν Εἰ μὴ ἔστιν ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν, ἄρα καὶ οἱ κοιμηθέντες ἐν Χριστῷ ἀπώλοντο. οὐ γὰρ ἀσώματον ἀπ' ἀρχῆς ζωὴν ἔδωκεν ὁ θεὸς τῇ ψυχῇ, ἀλλ' εὐθὺς τὴν ἐν σώματι, εἰς τὸ σῶμα τὴν πνοὴν τῆς ζωῆς ἐμφυσήσας. 225 Ps 118,53 Τῷ μὲν ἁμαρτωλῷ γέλοιον ἦθος ἡ θεοσεβεία, τῷ δὲ θεοσεβεῖ φρικτὸν παρανομία, διότι προορᾷ τὸ φοβερὸν τῆς τιμωρίας. 226 Ps 118,54 Ἐμοὶ δέ, φησί, καὶ παραμυθία μόνη τὸ πρὸς τὰ σὰ βλέπειν κρίματα καὶ εὐθυμία τὰ προστάγματά σου δι' ᾠδῆς ἀναλαμβανόμενα καὶ εἰς εὐφροσύνην ἄγοντα τῇ μελῳδίᾳ. καὶ τοῦτο μόνον ἀγαθὸν οἰησάμην ὡς ἐν ξένῃ καὶ ἀλλοτρίᾳ κατοικήσει καὶ μηδὲν ἀγαθὸν ἔχειν ἀληθὲς δυναμένῃ, διότι τῷ ξένῳ τὰ οἴκοι ποθεινὰ καὶ πρὸ τῆς εἰς ταῦτα ἐπανόδου πάντα λυπηρά. 227 Ps 118,73 Θεὸς δὲ οὐ πλάστου δίκην ἀνθρώπου διαπλάττει κἂν πλάττειν λέγεται, ἀλλ' οἷον ἄν τις πλάττων ἐργάσηται, τοιοῦτον ἀποτελεῖ δυνάμει τῇ τὸν τοιόνδε σχηματισμὸν ἐνεργούσῃ· καὶ ἐπ' ἐκείνην δὲ τὴν πρώτην πλάσιν 32 ἀναφέρεσθαι δεῖ τὰς νῦν λεγομένας πλάσεις, οἷον καὶ τὸ Πρὸ τοῦ με πλάσαι σε ἐν κοιλίᾳ ἐπίσταμαί σε· καθὸ καὶ Ἰὼβ λέγει τὸ Πηλόν με ἔπλασας, τὴν ἐν τῷ Ἀδὰμ πηλοπλαστίαν δηλῶν ἐφ' ἑαυτοῦ. Αἴτησις δ' ἐπὶ τῆς ποιήσεως εὐχαριστία, μαλ' ἀκολούθως ἡ τῆς νοητικῆς δυνάμεως τῆς συνιέναι ποιούσης τὰς ἐντολάς. περὶ ταύτης καὶ ὁ Παῦλός φησι Νόει ἃ λέγω· δώσει γάρ σοι ὁ κύριος σύνεσιν ἐν πᾶσιν. ἀκόλουθον δὲ ὡς πρὸς δημιουργὸν τὸ αἴτημα οἱονεί· τοῦ σοῦ φρόντισον ποιήματος καὶ τελείωσον τῇ νοήσει τὸ ζῷον τὸ νοητικόν· καὶ ὃ πρὸς οἰκείωσιν τὴν σὴν παρεσκευάσας, τοῦτο διὰ τῆς σῆς γνώσεως τῶν βουλημάτων οἰκείωσαι. ἐπεὶ καὶ ἐξ ἀρχῆς προστάγματος ἄνθρωπος ἐδεήθη ὃ τῶν πολλῶν ἐπιταγμάτων αὐτῷ ἀνεπιδεῆ καθίσθη τὸν νοῦν, καὶ δὴ ἀποσφαλεὶς ἐκείνου πλειόνων δεῖται τῶν τὴν μείζονα πληρούντων ἔνδειαν. 228 Ps 118,74®76 Χωρὶς γὰρ τῆς ἐν πολλοῖς πονηροῖς γυμνασίας καὶ παρ' ἐλπίδα γινομένης θεοῦ βοηθείας οὐκ ἔστι βεβαίως ἄνθρωπον ἐν ἀρετῇ παγῆναι. εὐσάλευτοι γὰρ ἀγῶνος ἐπελθόντος οἱ ἀναγώνιστοι. τὴν οὖν ἐκ τῶν πολλῶν κακοπαθειῶν βεβαίωσιν ἐν αὐτῷ ἐπιγνούς, τὴν βεβαιωτικὴν θεοῦ πρόνοιαν ἀνυμνεῖ· εἶτα δὴ τὴν ἐκ τῶν πόνων ἀνάπαυσιν αἰτεῖ λέγων Γενηθήτω δὴ τὸ ἔλεός σου τοῦ παρακαλέσαι με κατὰ τὸ λόγιόν σου τῷ δούλῳ σου. 229 Ps 118,83 Ἴσως νεκροὶ μᾶλλον ἢ ζῶντες ὑπὸ τῶν κακώσεων γίνονται οἱ δίκαιοι ὡς ἀσκοῖς ἐοικέναι μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις ἀποψυχόμενοι καθάπερ πάχνη περιπηγνυμένη, τὸ δὲ θερμὸν καὶ πρακτικὸν προαιρούμενοι, ὡς ἀλλαχοῦ λέγει Ἐκάθισάν με ἐν σκοτεινοῖς ὡσεὶ νεκροὺς αἰῶνος· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τοσούτοις γινόμενος, φησί, τῆς θεοδιδάκτου δικαιοσύνης οὐκ ἀφιστάμην, ὥσπερ Ἰωσὴφ τὴν δικαίαν σωφροσύνην φυλάττων. 230 Ps 118,86.87 Ἐντολὰς τὰς ἐπαγγελίας καλεῖ. θαρρῶν, φησί, ταῖς σαῖς ἐπαγγελίαις καὶ τῇ τούτων ἀληθείᾳ ζητῶ τὴν παρὰ σοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ μου βοήθειαν. 231 Ps 118,88 Μὴ ἐκδοθῆναι ταῖς τῶν ἐπιβουλευόντων χερσὶν εἰς θάνατον ἀξιοῖ, ζωὴν αἰτῶν οὔπω τὴν αἰωνίαν ἀλλὰ τὴν παροῦσαν. οὐχ ὡς τέλος ταύτην αἰτεῖ ἀλλ' ὡς ἀγαθοῦ τέλους συναίτιον ἐσομένην, ὅτι ζήσας φησὶ Φυλάξω τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ προστάγματα, δι' ὧν καὶ τὴν αἰώνιον ἔστι περιποιήσασθαι ζωήν. 232 Ps 118,93 Τοῖς σοῖς νόμοις ἕψομαι, φησίν. ἕξω γὰρ ἐν αὐτοῖς τὴν ζωήν, καθὰ δή μοι καὶ εἴρηκας ὅτι Ὁ ποιήσας αὐτὰ ἄνθρωπος ζήσεται ἐν αὐτοῖς. ζῶν οὖν μόνος ὁ δίκαιος κἂν τεθνηκέναι δοκῇ, νεκροὶ δὲ οἱ ἄδικοι κἂν ζῆν φαίνωνται. οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἔχουσι τὴν τῆς ζωῆς σύστασιν ἐν αὐτοῖς τὴν δικαιοσύνην, οἱ δὲ ταύτην οὐκ ἔχοντες τοῖς οὐ παρ' ἑαυτῶν ἀλλ' ἔξωθεν κινουμένοις ἀψύχοις ἐοίκασιν, ὅτι δὴ τὸ ζωτικὸν αὐτῶν ἔξωθεν, καὶ οὐδὲ μίαν ζωὴν ἔχουσιν ἐν αὐτοῖς. διὸ καὶ ὁ κύριος αὐτὸς ὢν ἡ ὄντως δικαιοσύνη ἑαυτόν τε ἀποφαίνει τὴν ζωήν, καὶ τοὺς μὴ μετέχοντας αὐτοῦ ζωὴν οὐκ ἔχειν φησὶν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· καὶ ὅ γε θάνατος τοῦ σωτῆρος οὐ ζωὴ μόνον ἐστὶν ἀλλὰ καὶ ζωοποιὸς ἀνθρώπων ἐπιλύσει θανάτου γενόμενος. 233 Ps 118,97 Οἱ μὲν ἄδικοι καὶ τυφλώττουσι πρὸς τὸ τῆς δικαιοσύνης κάλλος καὶ τῶν περὶ αὐτῆς λόγων τὸ σεμνὸν
english: We learn, if indeed the soul is not a human. For if it had the truth of living in its own life, the dead would not need resuscitation. Therefore the Lord said to the dead to live as if they did not yet have life, except insofar as they are in the power of the life-giving God; and he says they are lost if they do not happen to have a resurrection, saying he will raise his own, so that the one from it might not be lost. And Paul similarly says, 'If there is no resurrection of the dead, then those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished' (1 Cor 15:17). For God did not give a life to the soul from the beginning as incorporeal, but immediately the one in the body, having breathed the breath of life into the body.

Regarding Psalm 118:53, to the sinner, godliness is a laughing matter, but to the God-fearing, lawlessness is a terror, because he foresees the dread of punishment. Regarding Psalm 118:54, he says, 'To me, also, the judgments looking toward your commandments are my only consolation, and your precepts, being taken up through song, bring cheer and lead to joy' (Ps 118:54). And I have known this alone as one who will dwell in a foreign and strange land and is truly unable to have any good, because for a stranger, houses are longed for, and before the return to these things, all is sorrowful.

Regarding Psalm 118:73, God does not twist the justice of man like a potter, even if it is said he twists; rather, whatever a potter works, he makes such by the power of the one working such a shape; and the present-day 'moldings' must be referred back to that first molding, such as 'Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you' (Jer 1:5); just as Job says, 'You formed me from clay' (Job 10:9), indicating the clay-molding in Adam regarding himself. Prayer regarding the making is thanksgiving, but following this is the power of the intellect which understands the commandments. Concerning this, Paul also says, 'Understand what I say: for the Lord will give you understanding in all things' (Rom 11:33). But treat the request as if toward a Creator: 'Care for your handiwork, and complete with intellect the living thing that is intellectual; and that which you prepared for indwelling with yourself, make it indwell through your knowledge of Your purposes.' Since from the beginning, man was in need of that which, of the many commands, made his mind unsuited to them, and indeed, having been made unstable, he needs those which fulfill the greater.

For without training in many evils and without the hope of God's helping, a man cannot stand firmly in virtue, for those competing are easily shaken when the struggle comes. Thus, he recognizes the strengthening from many sufferings, the strengthening of God's providence; then he asks for rest from his labors, saying, 'Let your mercy come that it may comfort me according to your word' (Ps 118:83).

Perhaps the righteous become more dead than living under afflictions, as if they resemble ascetics rather than men, losing their souls like dust being blown about, while choosing the hot and the practical way, as it is said elsewhere, 'I sat in darkness as if dead to the age' (Ps 118:84); but even while undergoing this, he says, I have not departed from God-taught righteousness, just as Joseph guarded righteous temperance. He calls the commandments 'promises.' He says, 'With courage, I seek the help from you, my God, through your promises and their truth' (Ps 118:86).

He asks for life, not yet eternal life, but the present life, worthy of not being handed over to the hands of the schemers unto death (Ps 118:88). He does not ask for this as an end, but as a means to a good end, for he says, 'I will guard the commands of God,' through which it is also possible to acquire eternal life. 'I will cling to your laws,' he says (Ps 118:93). For in them is life found, just as you have said to me, 'He who has made them, man, shall live in them.'

Thus the righteous lives alone even if he seems to have died, but the unrighteous are dead even if they seem to live. For the former have the constitution of life within them, which is righteousness, but those not having this resemble soulless things moved not by themselves but from without, because their life is from without, and they do not even have one life within them. Therefore the Lord himself, being truly righteousness, declares himself to be life, and says those not partaking of him do not have life within themselves; and the death of the Savior is not only life but is life-giving, becoming the release of men from death. The unrighteous, moreover, are blind to the beauty of righteousness and the majesty of the words concerning it.

source_text: καὶ εὐπρεπὲς οὐ καθορῶσιν, ὁ δὲ τούτους ἑλόμενος καὶ τούτων εἶναι βουληθείς, οὗτος καὶ μόνος ἐν συνέσει καθίσταται, ὅτι καὶ μόνοις τοῖς ἐρασταῖς ἑαυτῆς ἡ σοφία τὸ ἴδιον κάλλος ἀποκαλύπτει κατὰ τὸ Ἐράσθητι αὐτῆς, καὶ τιμήσει σε· τίμησον αὐτήν, ἵνα σε περιλάβῃ. 234 Ps 118,99.100 Πάντα διὰ μελέτης ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ καλὰ, ὅθεν καὶ τῇ τῆς μελέτης ἐπιτάσει συνεπεκτείνετο, ὡς διὰ ταύτης ὑπερβαίνειν τὸν πρεσβύτερον καὶ τὸν νέον καὶ τὸν μαθητὴν τοὺς διδασκάλους. 235 Ps 118,107 Ταπεινὸν καὶ ὑπήκοον ἑαυτὸν παριστὰς τὴν ἐπὶ τούτῳ σωτηρίαν αἰτεῖ παρὰ θεοῦ τοῦ ταπεινοῖς διδόντος χάριν καὶ τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτὸν ἐπαγγειλαμένου τὸν ἔλεον. 236 Ps 118,109.110 Μείζων τῆς προθυμίας ἀπόδειξις τὸ καὶ διὰ κινδύνων ἰόντα μὴ ἀφίστασθαι τοῦ νόμου καὶ ἐν ἐπιβουλαῖς ὄντα μὴ ἀφέλκεσθαι τῶν δικαίων ὀργῇ καὶ 33 παροξυσμῷ τῷ πρὸς τοὺς ἐπιβουλεύοντας, ὡς οὐκ ἐπλάνησε τὸν ∆αυὶδ ἡ τοῦ Σαοὺλ ἐπιβουλὴ πρὸς τὸ ἀμύνασθαι πρὸς τὸ προσῆκον. 237 Ps 118,111 Ἐπέτεινε τὴν ἔνδειξιν τῆς περὶ νόμον σπουδῆς, ὁπότε κλῆρον ἴδιον ἔφη τεθεῖσθαι τὸν νόμον, οὐ πρόσκαιρον ἀλλ' εἰς ἅπαν ἐν τούτῳ προσελόμενος ζῆν ὡς οὐχ ὑπό τι ζυγὸν ἀνάγκης ἀλλ' ἁγίως ἐν εὐφροσύνῃ ψυχῆς. τοῦτο γὰρ δὴ καὶ μόνιμον καὶ δυσμετάστατον ὅπερ εὐφροσύνῃ πράττεται. 238 Ps 118,113 Εἰ καὶ μὴ μισητοὶ καθὸ ἄνθρωποι, καθὸ καὶ θεῷ μισητοὺς λέγεσθαι τοὺς τοιούτους οὐκ ἀνάξιον θεῷ κατὰ τὸ Ἐμίσησας πάντας τοὺς ἐργαζομένους τὴν ἀνομίαν, ὥστε ἀπόδειξις μεγίστη τοῦ τὸν νόμον ἀγαπᾶν τὸ μισεῖν τοὺς παρηλλαγμένους τοῦ νόμου· διὸ καὶ τῷ Ἰωσαφὰτ ἡ πρὸς τὸν τοιοῦτον φιλία μέμψις ἐγένετο διὰ τοῦ προφήτου, ὅτι τὸν ὑπὸ θεοῦ μισούμενον ἠγάπα. 239 Ps 118,118.119 Θεοῦ μίμησιν ἐνδείκνυται. εἰ θεῷ τε ἐξευτέληται πᾶς ὁ τῶν δικαιωμάτων ἀποστατῶν ἐπὶ ματαίοις ἐνθυμήμασι, καὶ αὐτῷ καταφαίνονται στεμφύλων ἢ σκωρέας οὐδὲν τιμιώτεροι· διὸ καὶ πρὸς ἀγάπην τῶν θείων διατάξεων ἐπεγείρεται, τὸ μάταιον τῶν φαύλων εἰς προτροπὴν τῆς περὶ τὸ καλὸν ἐπιμελείας λαμβάνων. Ἡ δὲ Ε ἔκδοσις Εἰς οὐδὲν ἐλογίσθησαν. 240 Ps 118,122 Ἀνεξικακίᾳ θεοῦ τὸ ἐλλεῖπον ἀναπληροῦσθαι ποθεῖ, περιμένοντος αὐτοῦ τὴν ἔτι μέλλουσαν ἀγαθουργίαν οἷον ἐγγυωμένου ταύτην ὡς ἐκπληρωθησο μένην, καθάπερ οἱ τοὺς ὀφείλοντας ἐγγυώμενοι πρὸς τὸ μὴ ταῖς ἀπατήσεσι χαλεπῶς ὑποπίπτειν. Σύμμαχος Ἀνάδεξαί με τὸν δοῦλόν σου εἰς ἀγαθόν, ὁ δὲ Ἀκύλας καὶ ὁ Θεοδοτίων Ἐγγύησαι ἐκδεδώκασιν. 241 Ps 118,129 Οἱ μὲν ἄλλοι, φησί, χρυσίον θαυμάζουσι καὶ λίθους τιμίους, ἐγὼ δὲ θαυμάσιον καὶ μόνον καλὸν ἐπιστάμενος τὰ θεῖα προστάγματα τοῦτον ἔχομαι καὶ θησαυροῦ παντὸς μᾶλλον διαφυλάττω. 242 Ps 118,130 ∆ιανοίξεως δεῖται τὰ λόγια· διὸ καὶ ὁ κύριος διήνοιξε τὸν νοῦν τῶν μαθητῶν τοῦ συνιέναι τὰς γραφάς, καὶ τὴν δι' ἡδονῆς ἢ δόξης ἀπάτην ἀφίστησιν ἡ διὰ τῶν λόγων ἐνδιδομένη σύνεσις. 243 Ps 118,134 Τοῦτο δὲ αἰτεῖ, ἐπειδὴ καὶ δύσκολος ἐν ταραχαῖς καὶ λύπαις ἡ περὶ τὸν ὑγιῆ λόγον ἀκρίβεια. 244 Ps 118,139 Ὅρα τὴν ἔχθραν ἣν ἔχουσιν οἱ δίκαιοι. αὕτη δὲ ἦν πρὸς τὴν ἀδικίαν αὐτῶν καὶ τὴν λήθην τοῦ νόμου. 245 Ps 118,141 ∆ύναται μὲν κατὰ τὴν ἱστορίαν ἀναφέρεσθαι ἐπὶ τὸν ∆αυὶδ τὰ ἐγκείμενα λέγοντα αὐτὰ περὶ ἑαυτοῦ. βραχύτατος γὰρ ἦν πάντων τῶν Ἰεσσαὶ παίδων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξουδενώμενος. πάντων γοῦν τῶν ἀδελφῶν αὐτοῦ παραληφθέντων ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς εἰς ἣν ηὐτρέπισε Σαμουὴλ ἑστίαν, ὁ ∆αυὶδ ἐν τοῖς προβάτοις τοῦ πατρὸς ἦν οὐ παραληφθεὶς εἰς τὴν εὐωχίαν· ἀλλὰ καίτοι νεώτερος ὢν καὶ ἐξουδενώμενος τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτὸς ἔσχε ψήφῳ θεοῦ, ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἐπελέληστο τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ δικαιώματα. νεώτερος δὲ καὶ ὁ τοῖς θείοις λόγοις στοιχειούμενος καὶ ἐξουδενώμενος διὰ τὸ ταπεινοῦν ἑαυτόν, καὶ ὁ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν δὲ λαὸς κληθεὶς μετὰ τὸν πρεσβύτην καὶ πρωτότοκον Ἰσραὴλ φθέγξαιτο τὸ προκείμενον ῥητόν. ἐξευτελίζουσι γὰρ αὐτὸν οἱ
english: And they do not see it as becoming; but he who, desiring these things and being of these, is established alone in understanding, that even to those lovers of her wisdom reveals her own beauty according to 'She loved me' (Ps 118:99), and 'will honor you; honor her, so that she may take hold of you' (Ps 118:100).

All things through study are beautiful in man, whence also the command regarding study was extended, as if through this one were to surpass the elder and the younger and the disciple [surpassing] the teachers. Presenting himself humble and obedient, he asks for the salvation upon this from God, on account of the one giving to the humble and having promised mercy to those who love him (Ps 118:107).

A greater proof than readiness is to go even through dangers without departing from the law, and being in attacks, not to be pulled away from the righteous [path] by anger and provocation toward the attackers, just as Saul's attack did not lead David astray from defending what was fitting (Ps 118:109-110).

He extended the demonstration of zeal concerning the law, since he said the law was set as a proper inheritance, not for a season but to live in all things approaching this, as not under any yoke of necessity but holily in the joy of the soul. For this indeed is both lasting and difficult to change, that which is done in joy.

Even if they are not hated according to man, it is not worthy of God to be called hated according to God such as these, according to 'You hated all workers of iniquity' (Ps 118:113), so that it is a greatest proof of loving the law to hate those who have strayed from the law; therefore also for Jehoshaphat, friendship toward such a one became a reproach through the prophet, because he loved the one hated by God (Ps 118:118-119). It shows an imitation of God. If even to God all the apostate of the decrees is exhausted by vain thoughts, and to Him they are accused as crown-wearers or dung-gatherers, being no more honorable; therefore also toward the love of the divine...
Disorders are raised up, the vanity of evils for the purpose of exhortation, taking care regarding the good. And the E edition was nothing reckoned.

By the non-evilness of God, the lacking is intended to be filled, waiting for Him, the good-working which is still to come, just as one guaranteeing this as it is to be fulfilled, just as those guaranteeing debts do so so as not to fall hard by deceits (Ps 118:122). 'Ally, raise up your servant to good' (Ps 118:129), and Akylas and Theodotion have guaranteed.
Others, he says, marvel at gold and precious stones, but I, standing only upon the wonderful and the good, have this and more importantly preserve all the divine commands as a treasure (Ps 118:130).

The words need opening; therefore also the Lord opened the mind of the disciples to understand the Scriptures, and the understanding given through the words keeps them away from the deception of pleasure or glory (Ps 118:130).
This also is requested, since even in disturbances and sorrows, the precision regarding the healthy word is difficult (Ps 118:134).
See the enmity which the righteous have (Ps 118:139). And this was against their injustice and the forgetting of the law.

It is possible, according to history, to refer the things contained here to David, saying these things about himself. For he was the shortest of all the sons of Jesse, but also being despised. For all his brothers having been taken by the father to where Samuel had prepared the table, David was among his father's sheep, not having been taken to the feast; but even though being younger and despised, he himself obtained the kingdom by the will of God, since the rights of God had not been neglected. And he was younger, and he who is being instructed in the divine words and being despised because of humbling himself, and the people called from among the Gentiles after the elder and the firstborn of Israel, should have shouted out the spoken word.
